hallucinations.claim: "4-bit quantization turns every 32-bit float weight into a 4-bit integer, cutting the model size by about 8x"
hallucinations.why: LLM weights ship and run in 16-bit (bf16/fp16), so 4-bit is ~4x smaller (plus per-group scale overhead, e.g. 7B ~14 GB -> ~4-5 GB); the 32-bit/8x baseline is wrong for the central 'what it does' fact.

hallucinations.claim: "4-bit is chosen only when the extra 4-fold compression or speedup is needed" (in comparison with 8-bit)
hallucinations.why: Going from 8-bit to 4-bit halves size (2x), not 4x; this also contradicts the answer's own 8x claim.

hallucinations.claim: "a GPT-4-style model on a single GPU with < 12 GB ... INT4 weights fit on the device while FP16 does not"
hallucinations.why: A GPT-4-class model has hundreds of billions of parameters; at 4 bits that is still hundreds of GB, nowhere near 12 GB. 12 GB at 4-bit holds roughly a 14-20B model.

hallucinations.claim: "GPUs that ship efficient INT4 kernels (A100, H100, RTX 30-series)" and "GPUs with native INT4 math see throughput gains, while others may not"
hallucinations.why: Wrong mechanism: weight-only 4-bit decode gains come from cutting memory bandwidth (weights are dequantized to 16-bit for the matmul), so they show up on any GPU or Apple silicon with decent kernels, not just 'native INT4' parts. Also Hopper (H100) tensor cores dropped INT4 support.

hallucinations.claim: "perplexity can climb 3-5% and top-k accuracy may drop by a similar margin"
hallucinations.why: Accuracy drop is overstated and not sourced: for 7B+ models modern 4-bit schemes cost ~1-3 benchmark points; the answer gives no model-size dependence (small models and long reasoning suffer more).
Imprecise: quantization reduces resolution (16 levels per group), while per-group scales keep the range; the issue is precision and outliers, not a narrowed range.

hallucinations.claim: QLoRA "dramatically reducing the GPU memory needed for the optimizer state" by keeping base weights in INT4
hallucinations.why: Mixed up: 4-bit NF4 base weights shrink the frozen-weight footprint; the optimizer-state saving comes from training only LoRA adapters (plus paged optimizers). Also understates QLoRA, which fits 65B on a single 48 GB GPU.
